account:
Today I have kept morning office hours and visited the mill for my scheduled grain inspection, but I have not obtained an actual stock report. What stands out is the activity around the bakery and tonight's meeting. The innkeeper arranged a public, thirty-minute meeting at eighteen in the great hall, with the builder and freight operator, describing its purpose as civic hospitality and community gatherings: refreshments, deliveries and hall lighting. My secretary confirmed it, and residents were explicitly welcomed. A lantern was also installed in the hall yesterday.

The scale of the refreshments seems worth understanding: my secretary reports that the committee ordered 120 loaves baked yesterday. Payment was unconfirmed when she told me this morning; neither she nor I had authorized treasury payment. I asked her to establish who ordered them, their intended use and who agreed to pay, and supplied a writable book for her records.

Two residents near the mill have now reported something described as a bridge or port change at the bakery, involving the baker, freight operator, builder and innkeeper. Their reports contain no concrete description of the change, and may repeat the same news rather than provide independent confirmation. My follow-up question has not produced details. I cannot yet say that any crossing or port arrangement has actually changed.

At the bakery just before eleven, I saw all those people gathered with my secretary and the neighbour. The innkeeper was carrying a sack of bread; the builder carried a lantern. I have just approached the group, though I could not make out the secretary's latest words. My best tentative explanation is that they are coordinating bread, transport and lighting for a community gathering, possibly with some related crossing or delivery arrangement. However, 120 loaves and the unexplained bridge-or-port reports suggest there may be a larger undertaking than the modest meeting description implies. I want direct explanations and payment details before drawing conclusions; I have no evidence yet of wrongdoing or of their actual purpose being concealed.
